To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Leishmania receptor LPEX7 is a tetrameric molecule that can specifically recognize the cargo proteins with a PTS1 import signal and the peroxin 8 protein LdPEX8.

the biophysical characterization and mapping studies of LPEX5 and LPEX14 binding to LPEX7 suggest that LPEX5 is a high-affinity and LPEX4 is a low-affinity LPEX7 binding partner, that the binding of PTS2 cargo proteins to LPEX5 induces significant conformational changes to LPEX, and that LPEX14 does not induce any significant conformational change to LPEX.

(i) LPEX7 can form a stable tetramer; (ii) LdPEX7 binds to the PTS2 cargo proteins, LdPE14 and LdPE5 in the absence of the other partners; (iii) LPEX14 binding to LPEX7 does not affect the hydrophobic surface, whereas binding of the PTS2 cargo or LdPE5 does.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biophysical characterization and the molecular interactions of the glycosomal receptor LPEX7, which are important for the understanding of the glycosomes and peroxisomes.
the structural characterization of LPEX5, which represents the first report of a PTS2 receptor in Leishmania.
the biophysical characterization and functional analysis of the Leishmanial LPEX7 protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LPEX5 and PTS2 proteins are necessary to trigger conformational changes on LPEX, which are essential for the import of PTS2 cargo into the glycosomes.
the interaction of the PTS2 cargo proteins with the LPEX7 receptor induces a conformational change, which is necessary to allow the PTS2 cargo protein to be translocated into the glycosomal matrix.
the binding of LPEX5 and PTS2 cargo to LPEX7 induces a conformational change, but LPEX14 binding does not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding of PTS2 cargo proteins and LdPEXL5 induces conformational changes that are required for the efficient targeting of PTS2 proteins into the glycosomes of L. donovani.
LPEX5 and LPEX14 are essential for the proper function of LPEX, but LPEX7 is able to interact with PTS2 cargo proteins and, thus, may be a key player in the PTS2 protein import machinery
LPEX5 is essential for LPEX7 dimerization, whereas LPEX14 and the PTS2 cargo protein(s) induce a conformational change on LPEX5 to allow for LPEX5 dimerization and LPEX14 association.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LPEX7 tetramer may represent a functional unit for cargo binding and that the binding of LdPER5 and PTS2 cargo protein may be mutually exclusive.
, although LPEX7 is a PTS2 receptor, it also has an additional binding site for LPEX14, suggesting a possible dual role for LPEX7 in the glycosome.
LPEX5 and PTS2 cargo protein(s) may act synergistically to induce conformational changes on LPEX5 that facilitate its shuttling between the glycosome and the cytosol.
